Subject: Intermittent Aurora-13B response failures — quick note

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

Thanks again for the heads-up this morning. We detected a ~2.3% uplift in 5xx and timeout responses for the Aurora-13B model serving your account between 08:30–09:05 PDT. Most errors were 500/504 during multi-turn chat flows with long context (ctx > 8k tokens).

Immediate actions we took:
- Pinned your routing policy to the warm pool to reduce cold-starts.
- Temporarily routed heavy requests to the v-quantized variant (aurora-13b-q2) to avoid kernel fallback paths.
- Collected KV-cache and runtime traces for the affected interval (attached: aurora-traces-20270601.zip).

We’re continuing to monitor and I’ll keep you updated as we confirm stability. Apologies for the interruption — I know this impacts a production path for you.

Best,
Chloe Martin

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent Aurora-13B response failures — quick note

Chloe / Monica — quick engineering update from SRE traces:

- Root symptom: an increase in kernel fallback for attention matrix allocation on the aurora-13b single-node tasks when seq_len > 12k (we saw OOM-like retry behavior resulting in 500/504).
- Amplifier: ClearPath production retry pattern (short backoff) led to request bursts that exacerbated contention on a small subset of GPU hosts.
- Mitigations applied at 09:20 PDT: re-route traffic away from 3 hosts with repeated kernel fallback, enabled a transient backpressure flag (rate-limit 40rps per customer route), and warmed cold KV caches for long-history sessions.

I attached a trimmed request log (clearpath-request-logs.txt) and full traces zip. No evidence of data integrity issues; this appears runtime/alloc related.

Next steps
- Short term: keep steady-state routing to quantized variant for 24 hours and monitor QoE metrics (we’ll compare logits/sample-level diffs).
- Medium term: schedule a targeted kernel patch for attention allocator and expand the warm-pool share for customers with >1M token/day.

—Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay — quick reply on quality: we ran a 200-sample diff between aurora-13b and aurora-13b-q2 for the affected prompt archetype. Average log-probability delta is negligible and there were no semantic regressions in our eval set. We will keep monitoring but initial QA looks acceptable for a temporary routing decision.

Also, we left the transient customer rate-limit conservative to avoid downstream retries compounding the issue. If you want, we can increase the ceiling once the warm pool fills.

Regards,
Monica Patel

Subject: Summary & follow-ups: Aurora-13B elevated errors (June 1)

Sanjay / Elena — final update and next steps after 24h monitoring:

What happened (summary):
- On 2027-06-01 08:30–09:05 PDT we observed elevated 5xx/timeouts for Aurora-13B on a subset of hosts handling long-context batched requests. Kernel fallback for attention allocation led to transient failures; request-retry patterns amplified the effect for ClearPath.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Re-routed ClearPath to aurora-13b-q2 (quantized variant) and routed traffic away from three problematic hosts.
- Enabled transient per-route rate limiting to reduce retry amplification.
- Warmed KV caches for long-history sessions.

Customer impact:
- ClearPath experienced a 2–3% error rate on affected requests during the spike window. No user data exposure; no model outputs were corrupted.

Planned follow-ups (owner -> ETA):
- Kernel allocator patch roll (engineering): Ben Carter -> 2027-06-10
- Warm-pool sizing adjustment (infra): Dylan Brooks -> 2027-06-04
- QoE regression check after full traffic shift back to float model (QA): Monica Patel -> 2027-06-03

Attachments: aurora-traces-20270601.zip (host traces), clearpath-request-logs.txt (sampled requests).

If you want a joint postmortem call with your engineering team, we can set aside 30 minutes tomorrow — suggest 10:00 PDT.

Thanks again for the patience and the quick signal that made this visible.

Best,
Chloe Martin
